title: Guess, then decode
prompt:
Four lines, four conversions between letters, numbers and switch patterns. Before you run anything, write your guess for each line in the comment beside it.

Then run `python3 decode.py` and compare.
hints: `bin()` writes a number as a string of 0s and 1s with `0b` in front, so `bin(3)` is `'0b11'` [py-038].
In ASCII, capital A is 65 [py-037]. `ord()` gives a character's number, and `chr()` goes the other way [py-040].
For `chr(66)`, set the Bit Board toy to 66 (64 + 2) and read the character it shows.
explain_after: `bin()` wrote 65 in base 2 [py-038], and `int(..., base=2)` read it back [py-039]. `ord()` and `chr()` convert between a character and its code point [py-040]. Capital A is 65 [py-037].
